meta.note: The two-day window overlaps with the last edition (23 September). General AI news (Meta Muse, Gemini Live Avatar, orbital data centres, the OpenAI agent breach in Australia) dominated the international feeds without a link to creative work. The State of Brand sitemap returned no pages inside the window. No Craft & Judgment piece from international sources passed the filter.

stories.title: A prototyping kit generated from specs, not prompted component by component
stories.blurb: Nathan Curtis describes a script that turns Figma component specs into React and web-component code (typed contract, styles, stories) in seconds, replacing weeks design technologists spent building a prototyping kit one component at a time with agents. What he values most is the side effect: an emitter cannot ask what you meant, so every undocumented convention in the specs surfaced and had to be written down.

stories.title: The source of truth bounces between Figma and code
stories.blurb: Responding to Tony Ward, TJ Pitre argues that once AI makes switching between Figma and code cheap, a fixed source of truth stops being useful: work moves back and forth until it holds up in the product. He adds that in teams with ten engineers per designer, code becomes the source by default, whether anyone chose it or not.

sources.name: TJ Pitre
sources.headline: The Source of Truth Is a Ping-Pong Ball

stories.title: Build the outcome, not another tool
stories.blurb: In his AI newsroom Exposit, Luke Wroblewski saw on-demand personalised reports quickly become the dominant way people used the site, ahead of classic news-site navigation. His test question for AI product work: are you building another tool, or delivering the outcome the tool was supposed to produce?

sources.name: Luke Wroblewski
sources.headline: Skip the Tools, Make the Outcomes

stories.title: The Ordinary puts 49 empty beauty buzzwords into a periodic table
stories.blurb: Uncommon's D&AD Black Pencil work collects terms like 'elixir' and 'flawless', checked with scientists to have no scientific or regulated basis, in a deliberately plain monochrome table. Nils Leonard says the team dropped scientific graphic language for fear people wouldn't get it; the brand reports an 11.8x rise in website traffic.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Beauty brands were writing AI slop before AI: here's how Uncommon won a D&AD Black Pencil for calling it out

stories.title: A new name when the old one works against the offer
stories.blurb: Vancouver's YWCA Hotel had become a boutique hotel, yet the name kept people assuming it was a shelter or a women's residence. Rethink replaced the name instead of explaining it: Hotel Willo, after the native willow, with a symbol simple enough to work on key cards and door tags.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: From YWCA to Hotel Willo: how Rethink solved one of branding's trickiest problems

stories.title: An AI brand that rules out AI imagery to stand apart
stories.blurb: Kiss Branding showed AutogenAI a single page of competitor logos to make the category's sameness visible, then drew on white papers and academic publishing and banned AI-generated imagery from the brand. The system splits into a rich editorial mode for executives and a stripped-back black-and-white mode for technical buyers.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Kiss Branding crafts mature new identity for enterprise AI platform AutogenAI

stories.title: McLaren takes its new wordmark from the family garage sign
stories.blurb: The evolved identity now covers both road cars and racing, with a wordmark based on the hand-painted sign above the McLaren family service station in Auckland. Speedmark, Papaya orange and the Speedy Kiwi stay, the colour palette gets wider.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: McLaren evolves its identity with a wordmark inspired by Bruce McLaren's family garage

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: McLaren Marks the Next Chapter with the Reveal of an Evolved Identity

stories.title: Worcester, not London, tops a ranking of UK creative cities
stories.blurb: Affinity's Creative Cities Index ranks 50 UK locations per 10,000 residents on creative space, job opportunities and affordability. In a Design Week Q&A, Deanna German concedes the per-capita data doesn't capture the full picture of working there, but expects regional cities to hold on to more talent.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: The death of the London creative monopoly? Q A with Deanna German

stories.title: Canva adds over 1,000 Monotype styles, mostly for underserved scripts
stories.blurb: The expansion targets Arabic, Bengali, Hindi, Khmer, Lao, Thai and Vietnamese, languages that historically had few professional-quality fonts; Hindi alone gains 99 families. It takes Canva's font offering past 3,000.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Canva adds 1000+ new Monotype fonts for global creatives
